rows.text: His family has steadfastly denied the charges. question: The charges were denied by his family. True or False? answer: True
The charges were denied by his family? His family has steadfastly denied the charges. Therefore, the answer is yes.
"The charges were denied by his family"? "His family has steadfastly denied the charges.", so the answer is yes.
He'd gone. Philip had to get them back. His Dad would kill him if he found that he'd taken them. question: Philip had taken them. true, false, or neither? answer: true
Philip had taken them? He'd gone. Philip had to get them back. His Dad would kill him if he found that he'd taken them. Therefore, the answer is yes.
"Philip had taken them"? "He'd gone. Philip had to get them back. His Dad would kill him if he found that he'd taken them." Therefore, the answer is yes.
Room and board. He nailed boards across the windows. question: Is the word `board' used in the same way in the two sentences above? answer: no
"Room and board." / "He nailed boards across the windows.". Similar sense of "board"? No.
Room and board. He nailed boards across the windows. Does "board" have the same meaning in both sentences? No.
